title: "Students Performance Analysis"
author: "Sana"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=TRUE}
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(rstatix)
library(psych)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# 1. Load the data

```{r load-data}
df <- read.csv("C:/Users/User/Downloads/StudentsPerformance.csv")
head(df)
colnames(df)
```

# 2. Data cleaning & preprocessing

```{r preprocessing}
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Total Score` = math.score + reading.score + writing.score,
    `Average Score` = `Total Score` / 3,
    `Passing Status` = factor(ifelse(`Average Score` >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")),
    gender = as.factor(gender),
    lunch = as.factor(lunch),
    `test.preparation.course` = as.factor(`test.preparation.course`),
    `race.ethnicity` = as.factor(`race.ethnicity`),
    `parental.level.of.education` = as.factor(`parental.level.of.education`)
  )

print(colSums(is.na(df)))

zero_scorers <- df %>% 
  filter(math.score == 0 | reading.score == 0 | writing.score == 0)

n_zero <- nrow(zero_scorers)
cat("Number of students with at least one zero score:", n_zero, "\n")
if(n_zero > 0) head(zero_scorers)
```

# 3. Descriptive statistics

```{r descriptives}
describe(df[, c("math.score", "reading.score", "writing.score", "Total Score")])

par_table <- table(df$`parental.level.of.education`)
par_table
prop.table(par_table) * 100
```

# 4. Visualizations

```{r plots, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = `Total Score`)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 20, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(count * 20)), color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Total Student Performance Scores", 
       x = "Total Score (0-300)", y = "Frequency")

ggplot(df, aes(x = `parental.level.of.education`)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "orange") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Parental Education Levels", 
       x = "Parental Education", y = "Count")

ggplot(df, aes(x = lunch, y = math.score, fill = lunch)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Math Score Distribution by Lunch Type", 
       x = "Lunch Type", y = "Math Score")

ggplot(df, aes(x = reading.score, y = writing.score)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "Relationship between Reading and Writing Scores",
       x = "Reading Score", y = "Writing Score")
```

# 5. Inferential statistics

## A. T-test

```{r ttest}
leveneTest(`Total Score` ~ `test.preparation.course`, data = df)
t_result <- t.test(`Total Score` ~ `test.preparation.course`, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
print(t_result)
```

## B. ANOVA

```{r anova}
levene_result <- leveneTest(math.score ~ race.ethnicity, data = df)
print(levene_result)

anova_model <- aov(math.score ~ race.ethnicity, data = df)
summary(anova_model)

TukeyHSD(anova_model)
```

## C. Chi-square

```{r chisq}
cont_table <- table(df$gender, df$`Passing Status`)
cont_table
chisq.test(cont_table)
```

# 6. Correlation & Regression

## A. Correlation

```{r correlation}
numerical_vars <- df[, c("math.score", "reading.score", "writing.score", "Total Score")]
cor_matrix <- cor(numerical_vars)
round(cor_matrix, 2)

pairs.panels(numerical_vars)
```

## B. Regression

```{r regression}
reg_model <- lm(`Total Score` ~ math.score + reading.score + `test.preparation.course` + lunch, data = df)

summary(reg_model)
anova(reg_model)

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(reg_model, which = 1)
plot(reg_model, which = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```
